title: Tandem affinity purification protocol for isolation of protein complexes from Schizosaccharomyces pombe
protocol: Transfer the yeast cell powder into appropriate tubes.
Thaw the yeast cell powder on ice (∼2 min) and resuspend it in the ice-cold IPP150 buffer.
Use 3 mL of ice-cold IPP150 buffer per 1 g of the yeast cell powder.
Gently rotate the tubes with lysates on a rotatory wheel in the cold room (4°C) for 30 min.
Optional: Sonicate the samples using MSE Soniprep 150 set at 6 amplitude microns (5 cycles of 10 s and 30 s cooling periods in between).
Transfer the lysate to clean centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes at 40,000 g for 10 min at 4°C to remove cell debris.
Transfer the supernatant into a clean centrifuge tube and repeat centrifugation three more times (40,000 g, 10 min, 4°C).
Use pre-cooled large volume pipet to transfer protein extract into fresh and clean centrifuge tubes.
Transfer the clean protein extract into 50 mL Falcon tubes.
Filter the protein extract through a 0.22 μm filter before freezing in liquid nitrogen (optional).
Transfer 50 μL of protein extract in an ice-cold 1.5 mL tube and store at -20°C for future analysis (optional).
Take 500 μL of IgG beads and mix with 10 mL of ice-cold ddH2O in a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Spin the mixture (400 g, 4°C, 1 min) and remove the supernatant.
Wash the IgG beads with 5 mL of ice-cold IPP150 buffer.
Spin again at 400 g at 4°C for 1 min and remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the IgG beads in 2 mL of ice-cold IPP150 buffer without vortexing.
Mix resuspended IgG beads with protein extract.
Incubate the sample on a rotatory wheel at 4°C for 2 hours to allow proteins to bind to IgG beads.
Load the IgG beads with bound proteins onto an empty Econo-Pac chromatography column.
Drain by gravity flow.
Wash the beads with 20 volumes (10 mL) of ice-cold IPP150 buffer and with 5 volumes (2.5 mL) of ice-cold TCB.
Transfer the IgG beads with bound proteins into a clean 2 mL Eppendorf tube.
Adjust the volume to 1 mL with TCB.
Add additional 1 mL of TCB supplemented with 400 U of TEV protease.
Incubate the sample on a rotatory wheel at 16°C for 2 hours to allow the TEV protease to cleave the TAP-tag, thus releasing the proteins of interest from IgG beads.
Load the cleaved sample onto an empty Poly-Prep chromatography column and collect the flow-through fraction by gravity flow.
Gently overlay the beads with 200 μL of TCB and collect the flow-through by gravity flow.
Combine the flow-throughs and adjust the volume of the sample to 2 mL with TCB.
Mix 2 mL of flow-through fraction and 6 μL of 1 M CaCl2 to titrate the EDTA present in TCB.
Take 100-150 μL of calmodulin beads and mix with 10 mL of ice-cold ddH2O in a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Gently spin the mixture at 800 g, 4°C for 1 minute.
Wash the beads with 5 mL of ice-cold CBB1.
Spin again at 800 g at 7°C for 1 minute and remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the calmodulin beads in 6 mL of CBB1.
Mix resuspended calmodulin beads with flow-through fraction from step 12 in a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Gently incubate on rotatory wheel at 4°C for 2 hours.
Load the calmodulin beads with bound proteins onto an empty Poly-Prep chromatography column and collect them by gravity flow.
Wash the calmodulin beads with bound proteins using 10 volumes of ice-cold CBB1.
Wash the calmodulin beads with 5 volumes of ice-cold CBB2.
Elute the proteins bound to Calmodulin beads using 100-150 μL of EB.
Wait for 3-5 minutes after adding EB before collecting the eluate.
Collect 8-10 eluate fractions into Protein LoBind Eppendorf tubes.
Add 0.5 μL 1 M DTT (5 mM) to 100 μL of eluted fraction of interest.
Incubate for 30 min at 60°C to reduce the protein disulfide bonds.
Add 3 μL of 0.5 M iodoacetamide (15 mM) and incubate for 20 min at room temperature in dark to alkylate protein sulfhydryl functional groups.
Add 0.5 μL 1 M DTT and incubate 5 min at room temperature to quench the alkylation reaction.
Add 2 μL of 50 mM phosphatase inhibitors mix (1 mM each).
Add 4 μL of Sequencing trypsin solution (0.5 μg) and incubate the samples overnight at 37°C.
Insert a frit into a 200 μL pipetting tip.
Push the frit gently to its final place using a paper-clip wire.
Shorten the 200 μL column by cutting the tip below the frit.
Take a 2 mL screw cap tube and make a round hole in the cap to accommodate the microtip column.
Place the microtip column into the tube, ensuring there is a space between the tip and the bottom of the tube.
Add approximately 50 μL of 50% C18 resin slurry in acetonitrile (ACN) into the microtip column.
Mix the resin well before pipetting.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 1 min.
Discard the flow-through.
Add 100 μL of ACN to condition and settle the column.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 1 min.
Repeat the ACN conditioning step.
Discard the flow-through.
Add 100 μL of 0.1% trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) to equilibrate the column.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 1 min.
Repeat the 0.1% TFA equilibration step.
Discard the flow-through.
Apply the sample to the microtip column.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 90 s.
Discard the flow-through.
Add 100 μL of 0.1% TFA to wash the sample.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 1 min.
Discard the flow-through.
Repeat the 0.1% TFA washing step.
Unscrew the tube lid and place it with the microcolumn into a Protein LoBind Eppendorf tube.
Add 50 μL of TA70 to elute the peptides.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 1 min.
Repeat the elution step.
Pool the eluates.
Dry the eluted peptide sample in a vacuum evaporator.
